Bearing press or vice with drifts that bear on the outer race only
Snap-ring pliers or pick for the stopper ring

required_parts.name: Lower dust seals (2)
required_parts.purpose: Renewed whenever the lower bearing is disturbed.

required_parts.name: Lower bearing, upper bearing and stopper ring if worn
required_parts.purpose: Only replaced if the inspection finds roughness, play or damage.

required_parts.name: Shock assembly
required_parts.purpose: Only if the damper is bent, damaged or leaking.

prerequisites: Engine and exhaust cold.
No sparks or flames near the open fuel system.
critical_stop_conditions: Oil or gas leaking from the damper, or a bent or scored shaft: replace the shock assembly; never open or repair the damper.
Never heat, puncture or clamp the damper body: it holds high-pressure nitrogen.
Shock eye bore scored or oval: stop; the shock body is damaged.
Bike moving on the stand when the lower bolt is out: stop and secure it.
Fuel smell or leak at the hose joint after refit: do not ride until fixed.

steps.title: Record the shock settings
steps.instruction: Count the rebound clicks, the fast compression turns and the slow compression clicks by turning each adjuster gently in to its stop and back out to where it was. Measure and write down the installed spring length too.
verification: Clicker counts and installed spring length on the setup sheet.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a maintenance stand so the rear wheel is off the ground and the bike cannot tip.
verification: Bike stable, rear wheel off the ground.

steps.title: Take off the seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Remove the side cover bolts and pull both side covers off, then remove the seat bolts and slide the seat back and off. Keep each bolt with its part.
verification: Seat and both side covers off, bolts bagged by part.

steps.title: Take off the air scoops
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts holding each of the air scoops to the frame, radiator guard and tank, and lift both off without bending the plastic tabs.
verification: Both air scoops off.

steps.title: Empty the tank and unplug the fuel line
steps.instruction: Pump the fuel out through the filler. Lay a rag under and over the fuel hose joint first, because the line holds pressure and can spray. Release the hose connector by hand only (slide the holder and cover, press the two side buttons) and never lever it with tools. Unplug the fuel pump connector. Cap the open hose and the pump fitting so no dirt gets in.
verification: Tank drained, fuel hose and pump connector off, both open ends capped.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Remove the tank bolts and lift the tank away. Lean it against a wall or prop it on its side; never stand it on the fuel pump face.
verification: Tank off and stored resting off the pump face.

steps.title: Undo the shock lower mount
steps.instruction: Hold the swingarm up with one hand or a block so it cannot drop, then remove the shock lower bolt and pull the lower bolt.
verification: Lower bolt out, swingarm supported.

steps.title: Take the shock out
steps.instruction: Remove the shock upper bolt and bolt and lift the shock out of the frame.
verification: Shock out of the bike.

steps.title: Treat the damper as a sealed unit
steps.instruction: The damper body holds high-pressure nitrogen. Never open it, never heat it with a flame or heat gun, and never clamp, dent or deform the body or rod. Internal damper service (oil, seals, valving, nitrogen) is not a procedure available for this shock in this guide.
verification: Shock handled without heat, clamping or any attempt to open it.

steps.title: Inspect the damper
steps.instruction: Clean the shock and look at the shaft and body. A bent or scored shaft, or any oil or gas leak from the damper, means the complete shock assembly must be replaced.
verification: Shaft straight and unmarked, no oil or gas leak (if not, a new shock assembly is fitted and the spring and guides are moved across if they pass inspection).

steps.title: Take the spring off
steps.instruction: Loosen the locknut, then wind the adjusting nut back until the spring is free. Remove the lower spring guide, the upper spring guide and the spring.
verification: Spring and both guides off.

steps.title: Inspect spring, guides and bolts
steps.instruction: Check the spring for damage or wear marks, the spring guides for cracks or wear, and the two mounting bolts for bends, damage or worn shanks. Replace any part that fails. Measure the spring free length and write it down; you need it to set preload.
verification: Spring, guides and bolts serviceable or replaced.
Spring free length recorded.

steps.title: Check the eye bearings
steps.instruction: Turn the upper and lower bearings with a finger through their collars. Any roughness, play, pitting or a torn dust seal means the bearing and its seals are renewed.
verification: Bearing condition recorded.

branches.label: Bearings smooth, seals intact
branches.condition: Both eye bearings turn smoothly with no play, and all seals and collars are undamaged.

steps.title: Remove the upper bearing
steps.instruction: Pull off the upper collars. Press the upper bearing inward by its outer race just far enough to free the stopper ring, take the ring out, then press the bearing out by its outer race.
verification: Upper bearing and stopper ring out.

steps.title: Remove the lower bearing
steps.instruction: Prise out both lower dust seals and take out the collars and bushing. Press the lower bearing out by its outer race only.
verification: Lower bearing, bushing, collars and seals out.

steps.title: Clean the eyes
steps.instruction: Clean both shock eyes and inspect the bores. A scored or oval bore where the bearing presses in means the shock body is damaged.
verification: Bores clean and undamaged.

steps.title: Grease the new parts
steps.instruction: Grease the lower bearing rollers and the dust seal lips with molybdenum disulfide grease. Keep grease off the bearing outer race; grease there wears the bore the bearing is pressed into. Grease the upper O-rings with molybdenum disulfide grease.
verification: Rollers and seal lips greased, outer race dry.

steps.title: Fit the upper bearing
steps.instruction: Press the upper bearing in squarely by its outer race until the stopper ring groove shows. Fit a new stopper ring into the groove, then push the bearing back until it sits against the ring. Fit the O-rings, collars.
verification: Upper bearing seated against the stopper ring.
Ring fully in its groove.

steps.title: Fit the lower bearing
steps.instruction: Press the lower bearing in by its outer race until its end sits 4.25 mm (0.17 in) below the face of the eye. Fit the bushing and collars, then new dust seals with their lips facing inward.
verification: Lower bearing depth measured at 4.25 mm.
Seal lips face inward.

steps.title: Fit the spring and set preload
steps.instruction: Fit the spring, the upper spring guide and the lower spring guide. Wind the adjusting nut in until the spring is shortened from its free length by the stock setting of 6.0 mm (allowed range: 1.5 mm to 18.0 mm shorter than free length). Each full turn of the nut changes the length by 1.5 mm (0.06 in). If you are restoring your own recorded setting, return to the installed length you wrote down instead.
verification: Installed spring length measured and recorded.

steps.title: Lock the preload
steps.instruction: Tighten the locknut against the adjusting nut to 10 N·m (7.2 lb·ft).
verification: Locknut tight, adjusting nut cannot turn.

steps.title: Grease the mounting bolts
steps.instruction: Coat the shanks and threads of the shock upper and lower bolts with molybdenum disulfide grease.
verification: Both bolts greased.

steps.title: Fit the shock
steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm and guide the shock into place. Fit the upper bolt from the right side and the lower bolt from the left side.
verification: Both bolts through, shock seated.

steps.title: Torque the shock mounts
steps.instruction: Tighten the shock upper bolt to 56 N·m (41 lb·ft) and the lower bolt to 53 N·m (39 lb·ft).
verification: Upper 56 N·m and lower 53 N·m done.

steps.title: Check the rear moves freely
steps.instruction: Lift and lower the swingarm through its travel by hand. It must move smoothly with no binding or knocking from the shock mounts.
verification: Smooth travel, no knock.

steps.title: Refit the tank and reconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Set the tank on the frame without trapping any wires or hoses and tighten the front bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft) and the rear bolt to 9 N·m (6.6 lb·ft). Remove the caps and push the fuel hose onto the pump fitting until it clicks, slide the connector cover back and fit the holder the right way round. Reconnect the fuel pump connector. Make sure the hose is not kinked or pinched.
verification: Tank bolts torqued.
Fuel hose clicked home, holder fitted, pump connector plugged in.

steps.title: Refit the air scoops, seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Fit both air scoops and tighten their bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Fit the seat, engaging its front hook first, and tighten the seat bolts to 22 N·m (16 lb·ft). Fit the side covers and tighten the side cover bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
verification: All panels on and torqued; seat does not move.

steps.title: Check for fuel leaks
steps.instruction: Refuel with fresh fuel. With the engine running at idle, look and smell around the hose joint and the pump flange for any leak, then stop the engine.
verification: No fuel leak at the hose joint or pump.

steps.title: Restore the clicker settings
steps.instruction: Set rebound, fast compression and slow compression back to the counts you recorded at the start.
verification: Clickers match the recorded counts.

steps.title: Bed in the shock
steps.instruction: A new or refreshed shock needs about 50 km (30 miles) of riding to settle. Check rider sag and the mount bolts after the first ride. If the damper itself is leaking or worn, the maker does not support opening it at home: take the shock to a suspension shop for a damper rebuild, or replace the shock assembly.
verification: Bed-in distance and post-ride check noted.

verification: Bearing condition recorded.

branches.label: Bearings smooth, seals intact
branches.condition: Both eye bearings turn smoothly with no play, and all seals and collars are undamaged.

steps.title: Remove the upper bushing
steps.instruction: Pull off the upper dust seals, collars and O-rings. Press the upper bushing inward by its outer race just far enough to free the stopper ring, take the ring out, then press the bushing out by its outer race.
verification: Upper bushing, stopper ring, seals, collars and O-rings out.

steps.title: Remove the lower bearing
steps.instruction: Prise out both lower dust seals and take out the collars and bushing. Press the lower bearing out by its outer race only.
verification: Lower bearing, bushing, collars and seals out.

steps.title: Clean the eyes
steps.instruction: Clean both shock eyes and inspect the bores. A scored or oval bore where the bearing presses in means the shock body is damaged.
verification: Bores clean and undamaged.

steps.title: Grease the new parts
steps.instruction: Grease the lower bearing rollers and the dust seal lips with molybdenum disulfide grease. Keep grease off the bearing outer race; grease there wears the bore the bearing is pressed into. Grease the upper O-rings with lithium-soap grease.
verification: Rollers and seal lips greased, outer race dry.

steps.title: Fit the upper bushing
steps.instruction: Press the upper bushing in squarely by its outer race until the stopper ring groove shows. Fit the stopper ring into the groove, then push the bushing back until it sits against the ring. Fit the O-rings, collars and dust seals.
verification: Upper bushing seated against the stopper ring.
Ring fully in its groove.

steps.title: Fit the lower bearing
steps.instruction: Press the lower bearing in by its outer race so that it sits at least 0.3 mm (0.01 in) below the eye face on each side. Fit the bushing and collars, then new dust seals with their lips facing inward.
verification: Lower bearing recessed at least 0.3 mm on both sides.
Seal lips face inward.

steps.title: Fit the spring and set preload
steps.instruction: Fit the spring, the upper spring guide and the lower spring guide. Wind the adjusting nut in until the spring is shortened from its free length by the stock setting of 8.0 mm (allowed range: 1.5 mm to 18.0 mm shorter than free length). Each full turn of the nut changes the length by 1.5 mm (0.06 in). If you are restoring your own recorded setting, return to the installed length you wrote down instead.
verification: Installed spring length measured and recorded.

steps.title: Lock the preload
steps.instruction: Tighten the locknut firmly against the adjusting nut (no torque value is published for this year).
verification: Locknut tight, adjusting nut cannot turn.

steps.title: Grease the mounting bolts
steps.instruction: Coat the shanks and threads of the shock upper and lower bolts with molybdenum disulfide grease.
verification: Both bolts greased.

steps.title: Fit the shock
steps.instruction: Lift the swingarm and guide the shock into place. Fit the upper bolt from the right side and the lower bolt from the left side.
verification: Both bolts through, shock seated.

steps.title: Torque the shock mounts
steps.instruction: Tighten the shock upper nut to 56 N·m (41 lb·ft) and the lower nut to 53 N·m (39 lb·ft).
verification: Upper 56 N·m and lower 53 N·m done.

steps.title: Check the rear moves freely
steps.instruction: Lift and lower the swingarm through its travel by hand. It must move smoothly with no binding or knocking from the shock mounts.
verification: Smooth travel, no knock.

steps.title: Refit the tank and reconnect the fuel line
steps.instruction: Set the tank on the frame without trapping any wires or hoses and tighten the front bolts to 8 N·m (5.9 lb·ft) and the tank screw to 4.0 N·m (3.0 lb·ft). Remove the caps and push the fuel hose onto the pump fitting until it clicks, slide the connector cover back and fit the holder the right way round. Reconnect the fuel pump connector. Make sure the hose is not kinked or pinched.
verification: Tank bolts torqued.
Fuel hose clicked home, holder fitted, pump connector plugged in.

steps.title: Refit the shrouds, seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Fit both shrouds and tighten their bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft). Fit the seat, engaging its front hook first, and tighten the seat bolts to 13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft). Fit the side covers and tighten the side cover bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
verification: All panels on and torqued; seat does not move.

steps.title: Check for fuel leaks
steps.instruction: Refuel with fresh fuel. With the engine running at idle, look and smell around the hose joint and the pump flange for any leak, then stop the engine.
verification: No fuel leak at the hose joint or pump.

steps.title: Restore the clicker settings
steps.instruction: Set rebound, fast compression and slow compression back to the counts you recorded at the start.
verification: Clickers match the recorded counts.

steps.title: Bed in the shock
steps.instruction: A new or refreshed shock needs about 50 km (30 miles) of riding to settle. Check rider sag and the mount bolts after the first ride. If the damper itself is leaking or worn, the maker does not support opening it at home: take the shock to a suspension shop for a damper rebuild, or replace the shock assembly.
verification: Bed-in distance and post-ride check noted.

exit_state: Shock refitted with mounts torqued, preload set and recorded, clickers restored, tank and bodywork refitted with no fuel leak.

steps.title: Record the shock settings
steps.instruction: Count the rebound clicks, the fast compression turns and the slow compression clicks by turning each adjuster gently in to its stop and back out to where it was. Measure and write down the installed spring length too.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a maintenance stand so the rear wheel is off the ground and the bike cannot tip.

steps.title: Take off the seat and side covers
steps.instruction: Remove the side cover bolts and pull both side covers off, then remove the seat bolts and slide the seat back and off. Keep each bolt with its part.
verification: Seat and both side covers off, bolts bagged by part.

steps.title: Take off the shrouds
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts holding each of the shrouds to the frame, radiator guard and tank, and lift both off without bending the plastic tabs.

steps.title: Empty the tank and unplug the fuel line
steps.instruction: Pump the fuel out through the filler. Lay a rag under and over the fuel hose joint first, because the line holds pressure and can spray. Release the hose connector by hand only (slide the holder and cover, press the two side buttons) and never lever it with tools. Unplug the fuel pump connector. Cap the open hose and the pump fitting so no dirt gets in.

steps.title: Lift the tank off
steps.instruction: Remove the tank bolts and lift the tank away. Lean it against a wall or prop it on its side; never stand it on the fuel pump face.
verification: Tank off and stored resting off the pump face.

steps.title: Undo the shock lower mount
steps.instruction: Hold the swingarm up with one hand or a block so it cannot drop, then remove the shock lower nut and pull the lower bolt.

steps.title: Take the shock out
steps.instruction: Remove the shock upper nut and bolt and lift the shock out of the frame.
verification: Shock out of the bike.

steps.title: Treat the damper as a sealed unit
steps.instruction: The damper body holds high-pressure nitrogen. Never open it, never heat it with a flame or heat gun, and never clamp, dent or deform the body or rod. Internal damper service (oil, seals, valving, nitrogen) is not a procedure available for this shock in this guide.

title: First start, break-in and post-break-in service after an engine rebuild
completeness: Covers pre-start checks, cooling pressure test after head work, first start, oil circulation and level checks, the two-stage break-in, oil and filter change with debris check, generator mounting check and the post-break-in chassis inspection. Fuel tank interior cleaning is listed but its method is not detailed.
excluded: Fault diagnosis and repair of anything the checks find
Fuel tank interior cleaning method
Suspension setup

required_tools.name: Cooling system pressure tester with radiator adapter

required_parts.name: Engine oil
required_parts.purpose: Fresh oil for the post-break-in change.

required_parts.name: Oil filter element and cover O-ring
required_parts.purpose: Renewed at the post-break-in oil change.

required_parts.name: Drain bolt gasket
required_parts.purpose: Always renewed.

required_parts.name: Left crankcase cover gasket
required_parts.purpose: Renewed after the generator check.

required_parts.name: Foam air filter oil
required_parts.purpose: Air filter service before running.

prerequisites: Rebuild completed and signed off.
Ride in a safe, controlled area.
critical_stop_conditions: Oil not circulating at idle: stop the engine at once.
Metal chips or grit in the drained oil: split and inspect the crankcase before running again.
Cooling system does not hold test pressure: find and fix the leak before riding.
Never open the radiator cap while hot.
Any knock, smoke, overheating or leak during break-in: stop and investigate.

steps.title: Confirm the rebuild is finished
steps.instruction: Before the first start the engine must be fully assembled and refitted with every fastener torqued, valve clearances and cam timing checked, oil filled (0.90 L (0.95 US qt) after a full strip, or 0.64 L (0.68 US qt) if only the filter was changed), coolant filled and bled, and all controls connected. Write down which parts were replaced: cylinder, crankshaft, piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears. That list decides the break-in.
verification: Rebuild sign-off and list of replaced parts recorded.

steps.title: Service the air filter first
steps.instruction: Wash the foam element in filter cleaner, dry it, and work in fresh foam filter oil until it is evenly wet but not dripping. Too much oil makes starting hard. Refit it so the seal sits all round with no gap.
verification: Clean, oiled filter seated with no gap.

steps.title: Do the pre-start checks
steps.instruction: Check: coolant up to the filler neck and no leaks; fresh fuel and no leaks at the fuel line; oil visible in the check window; gears select in order with the clutch working smoothly; throttle snaps shut with 3.0–6.0 mm free play at the grip; front and rear brakes firm. Pull the clutch lever: free play at the lever end must be 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in). Adjust at the lever adjuster, or at the cable adjuster under the cover if there is not enough range, and tighten the cable locknut to 4.3 N·m (3.2 lb·ft). Chain slack 50–60 mm (1.97–2.36 in) on the stand, tyres at 100 kPa (15 psi) cold front and rear, steering turns freely with no play, fork and shock dry, and no cable snags when the bars are turned lock to lock.
verification: Every pre-start item checked and corrected.

steps.title: Crack the oil pressure check bolt
steps.instruction: Before starting, loosen the oil pressure check bolt slightly. Do not take it out: with the bolt removed, oil spouts out when the engine runs.
verification: Check bolt loosened, not removed.

steps.title: Start the engine
steps.instruction: Put the gearbox in neutral (or pull the clutch in). Below 15 °C (59 °F) push the starter knob fully in; do not touch the throttle while using it. Press the starter. Crank for no more than 10 seconds per try and wait a few seconds between tries. Once running, hold it at a steady 3000–5000 r/min for one to two minutes, then return the starter knob.
verification: Engine running.

steps.title: Check oil is circulating
steps.instruction: With the engine idling (do not rev it), oil must seep out of the check bolt within one minute. If no oil appears in one minute, stop the engine at once. Then tighten the check bolt to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: Oil seeped within one minute; check bolt torqued.

steps.title: Decide on the cooling pressure test
steps.instruction: If the head gasket, cylinder, water pump or any coolant hose was disturbed, the cooling system must be pressure-tested after a 3-minute warm-up.
verification: Pressure test needed: yes or no.

branches.label: Cooling system not disturbed
branches.condition: No head gasket, cylinder, water pump, radiator or coolant hose work was done.

steps.title: Warm up for the test
steps.instruction: Make sure the coolant was topped up to the upper level before starting. Let the engine idle for a total of 3 minutes, then stop it.
verification: Engine run 3 minutes and stopped.

steps.title: Fit the pressure tester
steps.instruction: Lay a thick rag over the radiator cap and turn it slowly to the first stop to let pressure escape. When the hissing stops, press down and remove it. Fit the cooling-system tester and its adapter to the filler neck.
verification: Tester fitted, cap released safely.

steps.title: Pressure-test the system
steps.instruction: Pump the tester to 196 kPa (27.9 psi) and no higher. The pressure must hold for 5–10 seconds. Look at the radiator, every hose joint and the head/cylinder area for weeping, and at the hoses for bulging.
verification: Test pressure held 5-10 s with no leak or bulge.

steps.title: Remove the tester
steps.instruction: Cover the tester connection with a rag before releasing it; coolant will spurt. Refit the radiator cap and top up the coolant once cold.
verification: Tester off, cap refitted.

steps.title: Check idle and leaks
steps.instruction: Start the engine again if it was stopped for the pressure test and let it reach running temperature. Idle should be 1900–2100 r/min. Look around the head, cylinder base, covers, drain bolts, oil filter cover and water pump for oil or coolant.
verification: Idle in range, no leaks.

steps.title: Check the oil level
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright on level ground, warm it 2–3 minutes, stop and wait about 1 minute. Oil must be above the minimum mark in the check window. Loosen the oil check bolt: if oil runs out, the level is too high; let it drain until it stops, then tighten the bolt to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Add oil if the level is at or below the minimum mark.
verification: Oil level within the marks.

steps.title: Pick the break-in for the parts replaced
steps.instruction: Replaced cylinder or crankshaft: run the full break-in of about an hour (20 minutes at half throttle or less, then 40 minutes at three-quarter throttle or less). Only piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears replaced: about 30 minutes at half throttle or less. Watch the engine closely throughout and stop for anything unusual.
verification: Break-in route chosen and recorded.

steps.title: Ride the first stage
steps.instruction: After warming up, ride for about 20 minutes at no more than half throttle (30 minutes if only piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears were replaced). The engine stops by itself after 7 minutes at idle; just restart it. Idle time does not count as break-in.
verification: Time and throttle limit recorded.

steps.title: First pit stop
steps.instruction: Stop the engine and check everything that was taken apart for looseness, and look for oil, coolant or fuel leaks. Fix anything found before riding on.
verification: Findings recorded; nothing loose or leaking.

branches.label: Only piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears replaced
branches.condition: The 30-minute half-throttle break-in is complete and no cylinder or crankshaft was replaced.

steps.title: Ride the second stage
steps.instruction: Ride for about 40 minutes at no more than three-quarter throttle.
verification: Time and throttle limit recorded.

steps.title: Thorough pit stop
steps.instruction: Check all mounted parts for looseness and leaks, then adjust what has bedded in: throttle and clutch cable stretch, brake free play, chain slack and loose spokes.
verification: Cables, brakes, chain and spokes checked and adjusted.

steps.title: Drain and inspect the oil
steps.instruction: With the bike upright on level ground, warm the engine a few minutes and stop it. Remove the oil filler cap and the drain bolt with its gasket and let it drain completely. Catch the oil in a clean pan and look through it for dirt and metal chips.
verification: Drained oil inspected; findings recorded.

steps.title: Act on what the oil shows
steps.instruction: Metal chips or grit in the oil mean something inside is wearing: the crankcase must be split and inspected before the engine is run again. Clean oil means carry on with the service.
verification: Decision recorded.

steps.title: Check the generator mounting
steps.instruction: With the oil still drained, mark and remove the shift pedal, then remove the left crankcase cover (7 bolts) and check that the generator rotor and the stator are tight and show no rub marks, and that the stator and pickup leads are plugged in. Refit the cover on its dowels with a new gasket and tighten the bolts in a criss-cross pattern to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Refit the shift pedal on its punch mark at 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft).
verification: Rotor and stator tight, cover refitted at 10 N·m.

steps.title: Renew the oil filter
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and the old element. Fit a new element and a new O-ring on the cover, then tighten the cover bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: New filter fitted, cover bolts 10 N·m.

steps.title: Refill the oil
steps.instruction: Fit the drain bolt with a new gasket and tighten it to 20 N·m (15 lb·ft). Pour in 0.64 L (0.68 US qt) of oil: Yamalube or an SAE 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 oil of API SG or higher meeting JASO MA. No additives, no CD-or-higher grade oils, no oils marked ENERGY CONSERVING II (they make the clutch slip). Refit the filler cap, then recheck the level as before.
verification: Drain bolts torqued, correct quantity and grade added, level correct.

steps.title: Inspect the engine after break-in
steps.instruction: Look for pressure leaks at the head and cylinder, oil at the crankcase and covers, and coolant leaks. Check the silencer body and its stay for cracks and leaks, and the engine mounting bolts and brackets for looseness.
verification: Engine, silencer and mounts checked.

steps.title: Inspect the chassis after break-in
steps.instruction: Check the welds and mountings of the frame, swingarm, linkage and brackets for cracks or looseness. Spin the wheels and check for runout; tighten loose spoke nipples to 2.5 N·m (1.8 lb·ft). Check the brake disc bolts (12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft)), brake fluid levels and the hoses for leaks, the fork and shock for oil leaks and secure mounts, and the rear sprocket nuts (42 N·m (31 lb·ft)).
verification: Chassis, wheels, brakes, suspension and sprocket checked.

steps.title: Lubricate and adjust the chain
steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand and in neutral, set the slack to 50–60 mm (1.97–2.36 in) with both adjusters turned equally. Tighten the rear axle nut to 134 N·m (100 lb·ft) and the chain puller locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft). Lubricate the chain.
verification: Chain slack in range; axle nut and locknuts torqued.

steps.title: Grease and adjust the cables
steps.instruction: Lubricate the throttle and clutch cables and reset the free play to the values in the pre-start check.
verification: Cables lubricated and adjusted.

steps.title: Clean the fuel tank
steps.instruction: After break-in the inside of the fuel tank is to be cleaned and the tank checked for leaks. The cleaning method is not detailed in this guide; have it done by someone equipped for fuel-tank cleaning, then record the result and check the tank and fuel line for leaks after refit.
verification: Tank cleaning and leak check recorded.

steps.title: Retighten the torque-check points
steps.instruction: Check each point with a torque wrench: engine mounting bolts upper 45 N·m (33 lb·ft), front 53 N·m (39 lb·ft), lower 53 N·m (39 lb·ft); engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft); rear frame bolts 38 N·m (28 lb·ft); pivot shaft nut 85 N·m (63 lb·ft); shock bolts upper 56 N·m (41 lb·ft), lower 53 N·m (39 lb·ft); connecting arm bolts 80 N·m (59 lb·ft); relay arm bolt at the swingarm 70 N·m (52 lb·ft); steering stem nut 145 N·m (107 lb·ft); upper and lower pinch bolts 21 N·m (15 lb·ft); upper handlebar holder bolts 28 N·m (21 lb·ft), lower holder nuts 40 N·m (30 lb·ft); front axle nut 112 N·m (83 lb·ft), front axle pinch bolts 21 N·m (15 lb·ft); rear axle nut 134 N·m (100 lb·ft); spokes 2.5 N·m (1.8 lb·ft); rear sprocket nuts 42 N·m (31 lb·ft); brake disc bolts 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft); front caliper bolts 28 N·m (21 lb·ft); brake hose union bolts 30 N·m (22 lb·ft); rear master cylinder bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft); brake pedal bolt 26 N·m (19 lb·ft); fuel pump bolts 4.0 N·m (3.0 lb·ft); seat bolts 22 N·m (16 lb·ft); tank front bolts 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft), rear bolt 9 N·m (6.6 lb·ft); shift pedal bolt 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft). branches.label: Cooling system not disturbed
branches.condition: No head gasket, cylinder, water pump, radiator or coolant hose work was done.

steps.title: Warm up for the test
steps.instruction: Make sure the coolant was topped up to the upper level before starting. Let the engine idle for a total of 3 minutes, then stop it.
verification: Engine run 3 minutes and stopped.

steps.title: Fit the pressure tester
steps.instruction: Lay a thick rag over the radiator cap and turn it slowly to the first stop to let pressure escape. When the hissing stops, press down and remove it. Fit the cooling-system tester and its adapter to the filler neck.
verification: Tester fitted, cap released safely.

steps.title: Pressure-test the system
steps.instruction: Pump the tester to 137.3 kPa (19.9 psi) and no higher. The pressure must hold for 5–10 seconds. Look at the radiator, every hose joint and the head/cylinder area for weeping, and at the hoses for bulging.
verification: Test pressure held 5-10 s with no leak or bulge.

steps.title: Remove the tester
steps.instruction: Cover the tester connection with a rag before releasing it; coolant will spurt. Refit the radiator cap and top up the coolant once cold.
verification: Tester off, cap refitted.

steps.title: Check idle and leaks
steps.instruction: Start the engine again if it was stopped for the pressure test and let it reach running temperature. Idle should be 1900–2100 r/min. Look around the head, cylinder base, covers, drain bolts, oil filter cover and water pump for oil or coolant.
verification: Idle in range, no leaks.

steps.title: Check the oil level
steps.instruction: Warm the engine about ten minutes until the oil reaches about 60 °C (140 °F) and stop it. Stand the bike upright on level ground, start it for ten seconds, stop it and wait a few minutes. The level must sit between the lower edge of the check window and the maximum mark; add oil if it is low.
verification: Oil level within the marks.

steps.title: Pick the break-in for the parts replaced
steps.instruction: Replaced cylinder or crankshaft: run the full break-in of about an hour (20 minutes at half throttle or less, then 40 minutes at three-quarter throttle or less). Only piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears replaced: about 30 minutes at half throttle or less. Watch the engine closely throughout and stop for anything unusual.
verification: Break-in route chosen and recorded.

steps.title: Ride the first stage
steps.instruction: After warming up, ride for about 20 minutes at no more than half throttle (30 minutes if only piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears were replaced).
verification: Time and throttle limit recorded.

steps.title: First pit stop
steps.instruction: Stop the engine and check everything that was taken apart for looseness, and look for oil, coolant or fuel leaks. Fix anything found before riding on.
verification: Findings recorded; nothing loose or leaking.

branches.label: Only piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears replaced
branches.condition: The 30-minute half-throttle break-in is complete and no cylinder or crankshaft was replaced.

steps.title: Ride the second stage
steps.instruction: Ride for about 40 minutes at no more than three-quarter throttle.
verification: Time and throttle limit recorded.

steps.title: Thorough pit stop
steps.instruction: Check all mounted parts for looseness and leaks, then adjust what has bedded in: throttle and clutch cable stretch, brake free play, chain slack and loose spokes.
verification: Cables, brakes, chain and spokes checked and adjusted.

steps.title: Drain and inspect the oil
steps.instruction: With the bike upright on level ground, warm the engine a few minutes and stop it. Remove the oil filler cap, the crankcase drain bolt and the oil tank drain bolt with their gaskets and let both drain completely. Catch the oil in a clean pan and look through it for dirt and metal chips.
verification: Drained oil inspected; findings recorded.

steps.title: Act on what the oil shows
steps.instruction: Metal chips or grit in the oil mean something inside is wearing: the crankcase must be split and inspected before the engine is run again. Clean oil means carry on with the service.
verification: Decision recorded.

steps.title: Check the generator mounting
steps.instruction: With the oil still drained, mark and remove the shift pedal, then remove the left crankcase cover (8 bolts) and check that the generator rotor and the stator are tight and show no rub marks, and that the stator and pickup leads are plugged in. Refit the cover on its dowels with a new gasket and tighten the bolts in a criss-cross pattern to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Refit the shift pedal on its punch mark at 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft).
verification: Rotor and stator tight, cover refitted at 10 N·m.

steps.title: Renew the oil filter
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and the old element. Fit a new element and a new O-ring on the cover, then tighten the cover bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
verification: New filter fitted, cover bolts 10 N·m.

steps.title: Refill the oil
steps.instruction: Fit both drain bolts with new gaskets: crankcase drain bolt 20 N·m (15 lb·ft), oil tank drain bolt 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Pour in 0.96 L (1.01 US qt) of oil: Yamalube or an SAE 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 oil of API SG or higher meeting JASO MA. No additives, no CD-or-higher grade oils, no oils marked ENERGY CONSERVING II (they make the clutch slip). Refit the filler cap with a new O-ring, then recheck the level as before.
verification: Drain bolts torqued, correct quantity and grade added, level correct.

steps.title: Inspect the engine after break-in
steps.instruction: Look for pressure leaks at the head and cylinder, oil at the crankcase and covers, and coolant leaks. Check the silencer body and its stay for cracks and leaks, and the engine mounting bolts and brackets for looseness.
verification: Engine, silencer and mounts checked.

steps.title: Inspect the chassis after break-in
steps.instruction: Check the welds and mountings of the frame, swingarm, linkage and brackets for cracks or looseness. Spin the wheels and check for runout; tighten loose spoke nipples to 2.5 N·m (1.8 lb·ft). Check the brake disc bolts (13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft)), brake fluid levels and the hoses for leaks, the fork and shock for oil leaks and secure mounts, and the rear sprocket nuts (40 N·m (30 lb·ft)).
verification: Chassis, wheels, brakes, suspension and sprocket checked.

steps.title: Lubricate and adjust the chain
steps.instruction: With the bike on the stand and in neutral, set the slack to 50–60 mm (1.97–2.36 in) with both adjusters turned equally. Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m (100 lb·ft) and the chain puller locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft). Lubricate the chain.
verification: Chain slack in range; axle nut and locknuts torqued.

steps.title: Grease and adjust the cables
steps.instruction: Lubricate the throttle cable and reset the free play to the values in the pre-start check.
verification: Cables lubricated and adjusted.

steps.title: Clean the fuel tank
steps.instruction: After break-in the inside of the fuel tank is to be cleaned and the tank checked for leaks. The cleaning method is not detailed in this guide; have it done by someone equipped for fuel-tank cleaning, then record the result and check the tank and fuel line for leaks after refit.
verification: Tank cleaning and leak check recorded.

steps.title: Retighten the torque-check points
steps.instruction: Check each point with a torque wrench: engine mounting bolts upper 45 N·m (33 lb·ft), front 55 N·m (41 lb·ft), lower 53 N·m (39 lb·ft); engine bracket bolts 34 N·m (25 lb·ft); rear frame bolts 38 N·m (28 lb·ft); pivot shaft nut 75 N·m (55 lb·ft); shock nuts upper 56 N·m (41 lb·ft), lower 53 N·m (39 lb·ft); connecting arm nuts 80 N·m (59 lb·ft); relay arm nut at the swingarm 70 N·m (52 lb·ft); steering stem nut 145 N·m (107 lb·ft); upper and lower pinch bolts 21 N·m (15 lb·ft); upper handlebar holder bolts 28 N·m (21 lb·ft), lower holder nuts 40 N·m (30 lb·ft); front axle nut 115 N·m (85 lb·ft), front axle pinch bolts 21 N·m (15 lb·ft); rear axle nut 135 N·m (100 lb·ft); spokes 2.5 N·m (1.8 lb·ft); rear sprocket nuts 40 N·m (30 lb·ft); brake disc bolts 13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft); front caliper bolts 28 N·m (21 lb·ft); brake hose union bolts 30 N·m (22 lb·ft); rear master cylinder bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft); brake pedal bolt 26 N·m (19 lb·ft); Clutch hose union bolt 30 N·m (22 lb·ft). fuel pump bolts 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft); seat bolts 13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft); tank front bolts 8 N·m (5.9 lb·ft), tank screw 4.0 N·m (3.0 lb·ft); shift pedal bolt 12 N·m (8.9 lb·ft). Do not open hydraulic unions just to check them.
verification: Every torque-check point checked and recorded.

steps.title: Grease and oil the lubrication points
steps.instruction: Grease the pivot points, cables and lever and pedal pivots that call for it, and lubricate the drive chain.
verification: Lubrication points done.

steps.title: Sign off
steps.instruction: Re-service the air filter, repeat the pre-start checks, and record the bike as ready to ride only when every step above is done and nothing is left open.
verification: All checks complete and recorded.
